A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICTone and TST100K research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, tone-scorer evaluations, filtering and reward-learning ablations, a 20-participant user study, and additional experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative and qualitative comparisons with additional methods.

M1.justification: The two-stage tone scorer, dataset-filtering procedure, FLUX.1 Fill in-context model, training losses and inference procedure remain unchanged. The architecture and LUT-based high-resolution processing were already documented in v1, including Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same source datasets, TST100K training data, TST2K and PST50 benchmarks, and IFFI scorer evaluation. Reference-guided colorization and the illustrated scene categories already appear in v1; v2 adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 6 add CSGO and Nano Banana2. Table 4 adds CSD, which was previously cited but not evaluated there. Existing comparators are retained, while the seven-method user study and appendix comparison tables retain their original membership.

E3.justification: The reported preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations and sampling settings are unchanged. The user study still uses 20 image pairs and 20 participants. Added comparator results use the existing evaluations; no revised evaluation protocol is specified.

E4.justification: The tone-scorer effectiveness analysis in Section 4.3.2 is extended with CSD retrieval and preference results, adding evidence about general versus tone-specific style representations. The filtering and reward-learning ablations, cross-dataset testing and appendix analyses otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty intervals or statistical significance tests. The user-study aggregation and point-estimate reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New comparator results are added without changing existing scores. In Table 1, CSGO's PST50 Aes of 0.3607 exceeds ICTone's 0.2820 and GT's 0.3305. Table 4 adds CSD Recall@1 of 63.13 and PAcc of 70.89. Figure 6 adds CSGO and Nano Banana2 outputs; appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same losses, mathematical definitions and optimization formulations. Added equation references and citations do not alter the mathematics; neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about TST100K/TST2K, the two-stage tone scorer, in-context transfer and state-of-the-art performance. Added comparisons support existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 attributes Nano Banana2's low content preservation to reference-foreground leakage and explains how CSGO's oversaturation can inflate aesthetic scores without improving fidelity. It interprets the CSD comparison as supporting tone-specific representations and adds an image-concatenation efficiency limitation. Aesthetic-filtering bias was already discussed in v1 Appendix E.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, training and inference details. v2 adds ICEdit attribution for the already reported four denoising steps and guidance scale of 50. The project-page hyperlink retains the same destination; no new reproducibility settings or resource access are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine references, including CSGO, Nano Banana2, PerTouch and DiffRetouch, and expands discussion of CSD through direct comparison. The central research positioning remains unchanged. UniChange and ICEdit publication updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: Several introductory paragraphs are rewritten, experimental explanations and grammar are refined, and comparison-method, limitations and acknowledgment paragraphs are added. Author affiliations and contribution markers change. The overall section structure and most main-text and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 gain comparator rows, and Figure 6 expands to include the new methods. Figures 4–5 move into a side-by-side arrangement, Table 2 moves, and appendix Figures 7–8 exchange order and numbering. Figure 6 loses its scene-panel labels despite retained textual panel references; other illustrations retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added transfer/editing baselines and CSD comparison strengthen comparative support for both ICTone and its scorer. The aesthetic-score qualification and computational limitation improve interpretation. These are limited gains: configurations for the new baselines are not detailed, and the user study does not include them. The core method and previously reported results remain unchanged.
